name: Jungle
notes: Dense, tangled seasonally-moist (monsoon) forest and rainforest edge: shorter canopy than true rainforest, thick bamboo and giant-herb understory, vines. Drawn on Indo-Burma monsoon forest, SE Asian secondary jungle, Amazon bamboo forest and Congo-margin secondary growth.

canopy.silhouette: single trunk with huge ragged fishtail fronds

growth.juvenile_note: The first seedling leaves are small undivided bifid blades with ragged (bitten-off) tips; for a few years it is a stemless rosette while the trunk base widens. Later leaves become huge twice-pinnate fronds of wedge-shaped 'fishtail' leaflets. A single smooth ringed trunk then rises; at ~15 years it flowers from the top downward for several years and dies.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Caryota urens (to 20 m, flowers after ~15 yr, hapaxanthic: no new leaves after first inflorescence, flowers top-down for several years then dies; fruit dark scarlet-red, 32-38 weeks to develop, 2 seeds; fresh seed germinates well, viable 30-90 days); Palmpedia (bifid eophylls)

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (huge pendent once-branched inflorescences like horse tails, protandrous triads of 2 male + 1 female flowers, each inflorescence ~6 weeks in flower; fruit 32-38 weeks, scarlet-red); Palmweb (globose fruit ~1.5-2 cm, mesocarp full of irritant needle crystals)

canopy.silhouette: tall straight dark bole, dense rounded crown

growth.juvenile_note: Seed germinates within days of falling at the start of the monsoon, sometimes still on the tree; 2 thick, unequal fleshy cotyledons, then broad shiny leaves. Young sal is famous for 'die-back': the shoot dies back to the ground in drought, frost or fire for several years while the taproot grows, then one shoot escapes and grows away as a straight whip. Coppices freely.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Database (up to 6 m at 6 yr, mature 18-32 m; fruits regularly from ~15 yr; seed dead within 2 weeks; needs much light; coppices); Troup, Silviculture of Indian Trees (seedling die-back; seedlings bear moderate shade); Wikipedia (to 40 m); lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: Atluri et al. 2004 Current Science (sal: explosive pollen release, wind pollination with insect visitors, mixed mating); ICRAF/Troup (creamy fragrant flowers in big panicles Feb-Apr; ovoid nut with 5 unequal wings to ~7 cm ripens May-June; good seed years every 3-5 yr); seeds pressed for sal butter and eaten as famine food

canopy.silhouette: straight bole, open crown of huge leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two rounded cotyledons, then pairs of rough, hairy, opposite leaves that on vigorous saplings and coppice shoots are huge (60 cm or more). The sapling is a fast, straight whip with a four-angled stem and a few pairs of giant leaves, often several metres tall in 2-3 years, before it forks and spreads into a tall tree with a rounded crown.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Tectona grandis: 13 m at 5 yr, 16.5 m at 10, 21.5 m at 20, up to 45 m at 80; first flowering usually at 8-10 yr; very strong light demander; rotation ~80 yr); Wikipedia Teak (germination 15-30 days after pretreatment; Kannimara teak ~47.5 m, 450-500 yr old).

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (flowers Jun-Sep in Thailand; fruit mature ~4 months after fertilisation, Nov-Jan; natural fruit set 0.5-5%; bees the main pollinators; hard woody fruit in an inflated bladder-like calyx, 1,000-3,500 fruits/kg); Wikipedia (panicles 25-40 cm of small white fragrant flowers; fruit 1.2-1.8 cm). One-day flowers, crop, decay estimated.

canopy.silhouette: candelabra of pale stems, umbrella leaf tufts

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds wait in the soil until a gap opens. The seedling's first leaves are small and simple or barely lobed; each new leaf is larger and more deeply cut until the huge umbrella-like palmate leaves (deep lobes, pale undersides) appear. It shoots up as an unbranched hollow pole topped by a tuft of big leaves, with stilt roots at the base, branching candelabra-like only later.
growth.source: Alvarez-Buylla & Martinez-Ramos 1992 J. Ecol. (C. obtusifolia demography: fast-growing gap pioneer); Vazquez-Yanes & Smith 1982 (light-triggered germination); Wikipedia Cecropia (germination needs full sun and fluctuating temperatures, seeds viable >5 yr in soil, 5-15 m); values estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Cecropia (dioecious; spikes in groups inside a spathe; mainly wind-pollinated via pendulous spikes, small beetles and flies secondary; achenes in fleshy perianths eaten by bats, birds, monkeys; up to a million seeds per tree); Berg & Franco-Rosselli 2005 Flora Neotropica 94; timings estimated

canopy.silhouette: stilt-rooted pale trunk, tiered umbrella crown

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds wait in the soil seed bank until a gap opens. The seedling's first leaves are simple and toothed, then palmately lobed, then the big umbrella-like leaves divided into 12-15 radiating leaflets on long stalks. The sapling is an unbranched pole topped by a rosette of these leaves, growing metres a year; stilt roots flare from the base and branching comes later into a flat, umbrella crown.
growth.source: Wikipedia (pioneer of disturbed forest; in Nigeria it formed a closed canopy at 10 m within five years; to 20-45 m); PROTA/Useful Tropical Plants (very fast growth, short life of ~15-25 yr, soil seed bank, light-demanding germination); juvenile leaf sequence estimated from Cecropia-like Urticaceae

fruiting.source: Estimated from PROTA/Useful Tropical Plants and Cecropia-group ecology: dioecious; one 'flower' here is a head of tiny flowers (males many small heads on branched stalks, females single heads) that grows into a soft, finger-like, greenish-yellow compound fruit eaten by chimpanzees, monkeys, bats, squirrels and birds; pulp edible

growth.juvenile_note: After a gregarious flowering, masses of grain-like seeds sprout within 1-3 weeks. The seedling is a grassy tuft of thin leafy shoots; each monsoon it sends up thicker, taller culms from a knot of short rhizomes until, after 5-8 years, full-size culms rise in about 3 months, zigzagging and armed with curved thorny branch clusters at the lower nodes.
growth.source: Wikipedia (culms 10-35 m, 3-20 cm thick, curved spines, up to 50 cm growth per night, 90 cm in 24 h at Kew 1855); Janzen 1976 Annu. Rev. Ecol. Syst. (gregarious flowering every ~32-45 yr, clumps die after seeding); culm lifespan and clump maturity estimated. lifespan_years is the culm.

shrub.silhouette: giant arrow-shaped leaves held up on stalks

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one small heart- to arrow-shaped leaf on a thin stalk from a pea-sized corm, then a low rosette of a few glossy green arrowhead leaves on long fleshy stalks. Within 1-2 years a thick, ringed, above-ground stem forms and suckers sprout at its base; leaves grow to 1-2 m, held nearly upright with the tip pointing up.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (Alocasia macrorrhizos: 2-4 m, occasionally 5; stems to 3 m or more and 20 cm thick; 400-600 days to mature; seed germinates best at 24 C; grows best in some shade, tolerates full sun and deep shade; thermogenic spadix, insect-pollinated). Germination days, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Estimated from Flora of China / PROSEA as recalled (inflorescences several together among the leaf bases, boat-shaped pale yellow-green spathe 13-35 cm; ovoid head of ~1 cm red berries exposed as the spathe tube splits) and Colocasiomyia fly pollination of Alocasia; Wikipedia: tissues full of raphides.

shrub.silhouette: huge clump of thick arching culms

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling is a grassy tuft of thin leafy shoots. Each rainy season the young clump sends up stouter culms than the year before, reaching full-size culms (up to ~30 m tall, 20-28 cm thick) after roughly a decade. New shoots are fat conical spears wrapped in large brown hairy sheaths that elongate up to 40 cm a day; culm branches and leaves appear only after the culm reaches full height.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dendrocalamus giganteus (to 30 m, record 42 m; culms to 28 cm thick; up to 40 cm/day, record 46 cm in 24 h at Peradeniya; dense clumps). Culm elongation time (~3-4 months), culm lifespan, clump build-up and gregarious flowering interval (reported ~40 yr) estimated from bamboo literature.

New culms shoot up in 4-6 months in hairy triangular sheaths, then branch; lower branches thorny.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Guadua angustifolia: flowering cycle ~30-35 yr); guadua forestry literature (new culms reach full height in ~4-6 months, mature and harvested at 4-6 yr, culms die at ~8-12 yr while the clump persists). Values partly estimated.

shrub.silhouette: fan of paddle leaves, hanging red-yellow bracts

growth.juvenile_note: Seed is slow and erratic (2-12 months). The seedling is a rolled shoot unfurling paddle-shaped, banana-like leaves; a creeping rhizome soon sends up more leafy shoots into a clump 1.5-4 m tall. Each mature shoot ends in one pendent chain of red, yellow-tipped boat-shaped bracts, flowers once and dies back, replaced by new shoots.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Heliconia rostrata: pendent inflorescence, flowers beneath the bracts with copious nectar for hummingbirds); Berry & Kress 1991, Heliconia: an identification guide. Germination and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Berry & Kress 1991 (hanging lobster-claw: pendent chain of up to ~35 red bracts tipped yellow-green, yellow flowers lasting one day, blue drupes); Wikipedia (hummingbird-pollinated). Colour given is the red bracts. Timings and counts estimated.

shrub.silhouette: clump of arching torn banana leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: the first leaves are small, narrow and lance-shaped, rolled round one another into a short soft pseudostem. Each new leaf is broader until the plant is a small copy of the adult with a green, often dark-blotched pseudostem. Each pseudostem flowers once and dies; narrow-leaved 'sword suckers' rise from the rhizome to replace it, so the clump lives on for decades.
growth.source: ProMusa and Simmonds 'Bananas' (pseudostem fruits ~1-1.5 yr after emergence and then dies; suckers replace it; seeds of wild bananas germinate slowly and erratically over weeks to months); timings from seed estimated

fruiting.source: ProMusa/Simmonds (hanging inflorescence from the top of the pseudostem; one purple-red bract lifts each day over a 'hand' of 12-20 tubular flowers, female hands first, then male; wild fruit short, curved, full of hard black seeds, little sweet pulp); nectar bats (Macroglossus, Eonycteris) and sunbirds pollinate; set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Young plants appear 6-7 weeks after spores land on burnt or disturbed bare soil: the first fronds are small, simple and lobed, becoming finely divided and adult-like after about 18 weeks. After up to 10 fronds a rhizome starts, which may grow 2 m in the first year; by year two the patch can be about 2 m across, sending up single, triangular, much-divided fronds from underground.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Pteridium aquilinum (young plants 6-7 weeks after spores shed; adult-like fronds after 18 weeks; rhizome to 217 cm in year 1; spores usually in the 3rd-4th season; cover under 5% below 25% of full sun); Wikipedia (individual rhizomes live up to 72 yr; colonies 650 to over 1,400 yr old).

ground.silhouette: dense upright grass with white fluffy plumes

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small upright tufts of flat, pale yellow-green leaves with a whitish, off-centre midrib and finely serrated edges. Within 3-6 weeks they form sharp-tipped white rhizomes that run outward and send up new shoots, so one seedling becomes a dense, knee- to waist-high sward; fluffy silvery-white plumes appear in spring or after fire or cutting.
growth.source: MacDonald cogongrass biology review (no seed dormancy, viability lost within 1 yr, light needed, rhizomes form 3-6 weeks after emergence, light compensation ~2% full sun, flowers late winter/spring and after disturbance, leaves to 1.2-1.5 m). Shoot lifespan and first-flowering age estimated; the rhizome clone persists indefinitely.

ground.silhouette: spiralled leafy canes with red cone

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single slender cane with leaves set in a rising spiral (the corkscrew habit of Costus), from a small rhizome. growth.source: Wikipedia Costus spicatus (herb to 1.8-2.1 m, leaves ~30 x 10 cm, short red cone with sequential red-orange flowers, ant-guarded seeds, Lesser Antilles/Hispaniola/Puerto Rico); TopTropicals (semi-shade, flowers much of the year); Costus seed germination and cane lifespan estimated from ginger growers
